prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the identification of its active form, which established the basis for incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-achievement B001 prize to Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. After the round-1 exchange I still find the scientific case strong on its own terms. Holst established in humans that GLP-1 is a glucose-dependent incretin, Mojsov identified and synthesized the biologically active GLP-1(7-36) form, and Drucker mapped proglucagon-derived peptide biology and carried the therapeutic concept forward. Each name maps onto a distinct step, which is not true of B039 or B003. Independent replication across many laboratories and large randomized outcome trials in glycaemia, weight, and cardiovascular and renal endpoints settle maturity. Because the prize is for discovery, anchoring the citation on physiology and the identity of the active peptide keeps it a discovery prize and not a product prize. That also answers the chair's wording question: I would name type 2 diabetes and obesity, since both indications follow directly from the incretin mechanism and both are supported by trial evidence.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the weakness, and the chair is right that recollection is not a substitute for primary evidence. The priority for identifying the active peptide between Mojsov and the Habener group is not resolved by what we have been given, and I have not independently checked the primary papers. If the documentary record showed that Mojsov's contribution was clearly derivative, I would reconsider her seat. I have no documented ground to do so now. The Knudsen omission is the second cost: it is a judgement that discovery outranks development when only three seats exist, not a finding that her work is lesser. A prize framed on physiology also risks reading as passing over the people who made the medicines, and the committee should accept that cost explicitly. The same discovery-versus-development standard also explains why I keep B004 behind B045.

responses.point: Linnarsson agrees on the trio but says the Knudsen omission is not costless, that the citation must honour physiology and peptide identity without implying the drugs were the discovery, and that he would resist widening to four names at the expense of a clear citation.
responses.response: I agree with this and it is the position I am voting on. A fourth name is barred by the three-person cap, so the real question is whether any of the three should give way. I see no documented ground to remove Holst, Drucker or Mojsov, so the cost of Knudsen's exclusion should be stated openly instead of hidden by the citation. On your point about the CAR-T gap, I held that it was worse than the Habener question because the omitted person originated the concept. I still hold that, and it is why I keep B045 as an alternative and not as a rival to B001.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius said the Mojsov versus Habener priority question is the one point that could change her view of the trio, and she keeps B043 (Mori and Walter) as a serious fallback because of its clean attribution.
responses.response: I share your view that the Mojsov question is the pivotal one, and I would treat it as a test of evidence, not of reputation. Right now none of us has primary documents, so the conservative course is to rely on what is broadly accepted: Mojsov's synthesis and demonstration of GLP-1(7-36) as the active form, with the Habener group's contemporaneous work not erased but not clearly displacing hers. On B043, I agree it is the cleanest attribution on the shortlist and I would not dismiss it for limited translation. I still keep it out of my alternatives because B045 and B004 have shown clinical benefit, while a Mori and Walter prize is better judged in a later year when translation has matured. If B001 stalled on credit, I would take B043 seriously.

responses.point: Svenningsson, as chair, wants the B001 case to be judged on scientific grounds and not on the public profile of GLP-1 drugs, and he said he would move B003 or B043 up only if a tidy three-person allocation could be shown.
responses.response: I share the concern about visibility and have tried to test B001 against it: remove the public profile and the case still stands on human incretin physiology, peptide identification and outcome-trial confirmation. On B003, I do not see the tidy allocation you ask for. Cory, Adams, Strasser and Vaux contributed distinct things, Tsujimoto and Korsmeyer are outside the credited names, and apoptosis was recognised in 2002, so a clearly distinct achievement is needed. I cannot define one with three names, so I would not move B003 up this year. I would be open to reconsidering B043 in a future year if translation advanced.

responses.point: El-Manira said that, despite using optogenetic tools himself, he is wary of the attribution among Bamberg, Boyden, Miesenbock, Deisseroth, Nagel and Hegemann, and that the tool is less mature in medical consequence than GLP-1 or CAR-T.
responses.response: I accept the correction. My earlier trio of Deisseroth, Nagel and Hegemann was coherent as a technical lineage, but you and others have shown that six claimants against a cap of three makes any split contestable, and I cannot show it is not arbitrary. Your point that optogenetic clinical use is still nascent also weighs against it. I therefore do not propose B039 in any part of my configuration, and I would not use it as a second part. The standard I apply to B039, that a clean allocation must exist, is the same one I apply to B001, which is why I have stayed with the trio in which each name matches a distinct contribution.

uncertainties: Priority between Mojsov and the Habener group for identifying the active GLP-1 peptide is not resolved by the supplied record, and I have not verified primary documents.
Whether the committee will accept a discovery-only B001 trio without Knudsen, or will weigh the development step more heavily, is unresolved and would change the laureate set.
If B045 is ever needed, whether June and Sadelain alone, or with Rosenberg, is correct given the absence of Eshhar and Gross.
Whether the long-term safety of chronic GLP-1 therapy will change the clinical picture, although I regard it as peripheral to the discovery.
statement.conflict_note: No change since round 1. I have co-authored with Sten Linnarsson and Jonas Frisén and share an institution (Karolinska Institutet) with colleagues, but none of the credited names on any shortlisted ballot is documented as connected to me, and I do not request recusal.
